dead_key.fault: The {KEY} key no longer registers because its switch has failed; swap the switch.
dead_key.diagnosis: That sounds like a dead switch under the {KEY} key. We will unplug the board, pull the keycap and the switch, and drop in a new one.
safety_notes: Unplug the keyboard before pulling anything.
Touch grounded metal first to discharge static.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Pulling switches while the cable is still plugged in.

steps.title: Pull the keycap
steps.instruction: Slide the keycap puller under the {KEY} keycap and lift it straight up.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is off and the switch below it is visible.
common_mistakes: Prying at an angle and bending the stem.

steps.title: Place the switch puller
steps.instruction: Put the two prongs of the switch puller on the top and bottom clips of the {KEY} switch.
steps.expected_visual_state: A switch puller is gripping the {KEY} switch.
common_mistakes: Putting the prongs on the sides instead of the clips.

steps.title: Pull the switch
steps.instruction: Squeeze the puller and pull the switch straight up out of its socket.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} switch is out and the empty socket is visible.
common_mistakes: Twisting the switch and bending the pins.

steps.title: Check the socket
steps.instruction: Look into the empty socket and blow out any dust.
steps.expected_visual_state: The socket is clean and its two contacts are flat.
common_mistakes: Pressing on the socket contacts.

steps.title: Check the new switch
steps.instruction: Check the new switch's two pins are straight.
steps.expected_visual_state: The spare switch is held up with both pins straight.
common_mistakes: Fitting a switch with a bent pin.

steps.title: Line it up
steps.instruction: Hold the new switch over the socket with its pins over the holes.
steps.expected_visual_state: The spare switch hovers over the socket.
common_mistakes: Rotating the switch 180 degrees.

steps.title: Press it in
steps.instruction: Press the switch straight down until it clicks flush in the plate.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch sits flush in the plate.
common_mistakes: Pushing on one corner only.

steps.title: Refit the keycap
steps.instruction: Press the {KEY} keycap back on until it seats.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is on and level with its neighbours.
common_mistakes: Seating the keycap crooked.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and press the {KEY} key three times.
steps.expected_visual_state: The backlight is on and {KEY} types once per press.
common_mistakes: Testing before the keycap is seated.

sticky_key.fault: The {KEY} key is sticky or slow to spring back, usually from dust or a spill under the keycap.
sticky_key.diagnosis: A sticky {KEY} is usually dirt under the keycap. We will unplug the board, lift the keycap and blow the switch clean.
safety_notes: Never pour liquid into the keyboard.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged in and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Cleaning with the keyboard still powered.

steps.title: Pull the keycap
steps.instruction: Lift the {KEY} keycap straight up with the keycap puller.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is off and the switch is visible.
common_mistakes: Prying from one side.

steps.title: Blow it clean
steps.instruction: Give the {KEY} switch and the plate around it short puffs of compressed air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The area around the {KEY} switch is free of crumbs and dust.
common_mistakes: Holding the can upside down and spraying liquid.

steps.title: Test the stem
steps.instruction: Press the switch stem a few times to feel whether it springs back freely.
steps.expected_visual_state: A finger presses the switch stem and it springs back.
common_mistakes: Pressing with the keycap still half on.

steps.title: Refit the keycap
steps.instruction: Press the {KEY} keycap back on until it seats.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is on and level.
common_mistakes: Seating it crooked.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and press {KEY} three times.
steps.expected_visual_state: The backlight is on and {KEY} springs back each time.
common_mistakes: Skipping the final test.

missing_keycap.fault: The {KEY} keycap is missing or damaged and needs replacing.
missing_keycap.diagnosis: The {KEY} keycap needs a replacement. We will check the switch underneath is fine and press a new keycap on.
safety_notes: Unplug the keyboard while the switch is exposed.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged in and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving it plugged in while handling the exposed switch.

steps.title: Check the switch
steps.instruction: Look at the exposed {KEY} switch and check the stem is intact.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} switch is visible with an intact cross-shaped stem.
common_mistakes: Pressing the stem sideways.

steps.title: Fit the keycap
steps.instruction: Line the new keycap up over the {KEY} stem and press it straight down until it seats.
steps.expected_visual_state: A keycap sits level on the {KEY} switch.
common_mistakes: Pressing on one corner so the keycap tilts.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and press {KEY} three times.
steps.expected_visual_state: The backlight is on and {KEY} types once per press.
common_mistakes: Skipping the test.

spacebar_stabilizer.fault: The long {KEY} key rattles or sticks on one side because its stabilizer bar is loose or dirty.
spacebar_stabilizer.diagnosis: A rattling {KEY} is almost always the stabilizer bar underneath. We will lift the keycap and check the bar seats cleanly.
safety_notes: Lift long keycaps evenly so the stabilizer bar does not snap.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged in and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Working on the keyboard while powered.

steps.title: Pull the keycap
steps.instruction: Lift the {KEY} keycap straight up, working the puller along both ends so it comes off evenly.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is off and the stabilizer bar is visible.
common_mistakes: Lifting one end only and bending the stabilizer wire.

steps.title: Inspect the stabilizer
steps.instruction: Look at the stabilizer bar under the {KEY} key and check both ends sit in their housings.
steps.expected_visual_state: The stabilizer wire is visible under the {KEY} key with both ends seated.
common_mistakes: Bending the wire while checking it.

steps.title: Blow it clean
steps.instruction: Blow short puffs of compressed air along the bar and housings.
steps.expected_visual_state: The stabilizer bar and its housings are free of dust.
common_mistakes: Spraying liquid by tilting the can.

steps.title: Refit the keycap
steps.instruction: Press the {KEY} keycap back on evenly, with both ends clicking onto the stabilizer.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is on, level, and does not rock.
common_mistakes: Seating only one end of the stabilizer.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and press the {KEY} at both ends and the middle.
steps.expected_visual_state: The backlight is on and the {KEY} presses evenly without rattling.
common_mistakes: Only testing the middle of the key.

no_power.fault: The keyboard does not power on or is not detected, so the cable or USB-C port is suspect.
no_power.diagnosis: When a board will not power up, the cable or the port is the usual cause. We will check the cable first, then the port.
safety_notes: Do not force the plug into the port.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is out of the port.
common_mistakes: Yanking the cable at an angle.

steps.title: Inspect the port
steps.instruction: Look into the USB-C port at the back for lint or bent contacts.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is visible and clear of lint.
common_mistakes: Poking the contacts with metal.

steps.title: Swap the cable
steps.instruction: Try a different USB-C data cable and plug it in firmly.
steps.expected_visual_state: A different cable is fully seated in the port and the backlight comes on.
common_mistakes: Using a charge-only cable.

steps.title: Check the mode switch
steps.instruction: Check the mode switch is set to cable, not wireless.
steps.expected_visual_state: The mode switch is slid to the cable position.
common_mistakes: Leaving the switch on wireless.

backlight.fault: The backlight is dead or flickering.
backlight.diagnosis: A dead backlight is often just the lighting mode. We will check the cable and the lighting settings before opening anything.
safety_notes: Do not open the case on a keyboard that is plugged in.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is out and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Skipping the unplug before checking connections.

steps.title: Check the lights
steps.instruction: Look at the LEDs under the keys for any that look damaged or dark.
steps.expected_visual_state: The LEDs under the keys are visible and none are burnt.
common_mistakes: Touching the LEDs.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and cycle the lighting mode with the Function key combination in the manual.
steps.expected_visual_state: The backlight comes on and changes mode.
common_mistakes: Setting the brightness to zero.

steps.title: Check the cable
steps.instruction: If the lights stay off, try a second USB-C cable.
steps.expected_visual_state: A different cable is plugged in and the keyboard is powered.
common_mistakes: Testing with the same worn cable.

other_keyboard_fault.fault: A keyboard fault that needs a general inspection.
other_keyboard_fault.diagnosis: I am not sure what is wrong yet, so we will start by checking the cable and the key area.
safety_notes: Unplug the keyboard before touching anything inside.

steps.title: Unplug
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the keyboard.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is out and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Working while plugged in.

steps.title: Look at the keys
steps.instruction: Look across the key area for anything loose, cracked or out of place.
steps.expected_visual_state: The key area is visible and all keycaps sit level.
common_mistakes: Missing a keycap that sits slightly crooked.

steps.title: Check the port
steps.instruction: Check the USB-C port for lint or damage.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is visible and clear.
common_mistakes: Poking inside with metal.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and test the keys.
steps.expected_visual_state: The backlight is on and keys type.
common_mistakes: Skipping the test.
